title: Make queued VIXEN build paths independent of nested working directory
body: The provider build was first invoked from VIXEN and failed because build/wsl was not present at that relative location. Running the same queued command from the worktree root succeeded. The worker brief gives the queue command but assumes the caller knows the required cwd. Suggested consolidation: have the documented VIXEN queue entry resolve the worktree root or validate the required cwd before admission.

title: Document required tier and effort tags for SPT proposals
body: The proposal command documented in the worker rules with velocity and consolidation tags was rejected by the current SPT CLI until exactly one tier tag and one effort tag were also supplied. Both validation messages were required to discover the full schema. Suggested consolidation: keep the worker rules or proposal CLI help synchronized with the required tier and effort tags.

title: Expose the FidelityFX utility include in its message translation unit
body: The queued provider build command failed while compiling the vendored SDK source src/shared/ffx_message.cpp because it calls FFX_UNUSED without including the utility header that defines it. Adding the header to that translation unit fixes the focused VIXEN target. Suggested consolidation: include or model the FidelityFX shared utility dependency in the SDK target setup so isolated component builds do not rely on umbrella build state.

title: Declare the FidelityFX component include root for blob accessors
body: The queued provider build failed while compiling the pinned FSR3 shader blob accessor because its upstream include path is rooted at src/components, but the VIXEN static target only listed the fsr3upscaler child directory. Adding the parent source include root fixes that compile. Suggested consolidation: make the FidelityFX component target setup declare the SDK source include root expected by its blob accessors.

title: Normalize FidelityFX shader depfiles emitted through WSL interop
body: Each queued rebuild regenerates the FSR3 permutation headers although the GLSL inputs are unchanged. The FidelityFX compiler depfile uses absolute //wsl.localhost/Ubuntu paths while the CMake build uses /home paths, and the Windows-style paths are not being reused as stable dependencies. Suggested consolidation: normalize the emitted depfile paths or model the shader include tree explicitly so unchanged SDK shaders do not regenerate on every build.

title: Provide a Linux compatibility contract for FidelityFX SDK 1.1.4
body: The queued vixen_lookdev_capture build reached the pinned FidelityFX Vulkan sources and failed on Microsoft secure CRT APIs such as wcscpy_s, strcpy_s, sprintf_s and _countof, missing libc and codecvt declarations, and an FSR3 public context size smaller than the private context. A target-scoped non-Windows compatibility header plus a shared 1 MiB context-size override resolves those platform assumptions. Suggested consolidation: ship or generate the SDK portability layer and context-size contract as part of the provider integration.

title: Account for WSL interop compiler progress in the queue stall watchdog
body: The queued VIXEN build was killed at 200 seconds with CPU idle and output idle because the pinned FidelityFX Windows shader compiler was running as a WSL interop child and emitted output only after a permutation batch completed. Earlier batches from the same compiler completed after longer silent intervals. Setting UT_STALL_IDLE_HARD_S=900 before the queue wrapper provides an evidenced recovery route. Suggested consolidation: have the watchdog account for Windows child progress or document a per-job idle grace for these cross-platform compiler steps.

title: Separate the FidelityFX 1.1.4 Vulkan frame-generation callback from upscaler-only builds
body: ffxGetInterfaceVK unconditionally installs ffxSetFrameGenerationConfigToSwapchainVK, but this SDK checkout only declares the callback and leaves its implementation to a frame-generation integration. VIXEN had to add an upscaler-only fail-closed callback to link the backend. The SDK facade should expose a null or explicit unsupported callback for consumers that ship FSR3 upscaling without frame generation.

title: Expose an external-dispatch render-graph seam without a placeholder shader
body: The FSR3 module needs ComputeStageNode for graph ordering and GPU timing, but the node also requires a shader family and synthesized EASU dispatch even though the external FidelityFX recorder replaces that dispatch. Wiring a placeholder FSR1 shader by hand adds unrelated shader compilation and can mislead future providers. Suggested consolidation: let a graph stage declare an external command recorder as its execution implementation while retaining the standard image/resource and timing contracts.

title: Resolve the runtime profile before admitting an optional upscaler
body: UpscalerMachineProfile declares providerCompileSet, but provider selection consumes compiledAdapters and a Vulkan feature path without resolving a machine profile or intersecting its compile set. The wsl2-dozen profile excludes FSR3, yet the test qualification path can admit the compiled adapter on a Dozen device. Suggested consolidation: define the runtime profile identity inputs and make provider admission consume the resolved profile, so unsupported ICDs stay out before provider initialization.

title: Route provider initialization failure through the next upscaler candidate
body: BuildRenderGraph selects a provider before the live Vulkan device exists; the FFX context is created later during ComputeStageNode compile, where an initialization error currently throws out of graph compilation. That leaves no FSR1 then native fallback for a provider that fails initialization after selection, and the initialized eligibility bit currently reflects only a graph handle. Suggested consolidation: make successful provider initialization part of selection or provide a graph rebuild/fallback result that advances to the next candidate.

title: Define the FSR3 upscaler in its Vulkan blob target
body: The queued CMake build had FFX_FSR3UPSCALER unset for FidelityFXFsr3VK, so the generic permutation dispatcher compiled without an FSR3 branch and returned an empty shader blob. Adding the private target definition enables the FSR3 shader dispatch. Suggested consolidation: make component target options derive from the selected SDK component list.

title: Guard the optional Vulkan memory requirements function
body: On the Dozen adapter, FidelityFX reports dedicated allocation support while vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements2KHR is absent from its loaded function table; the SDK calls the null function pointer during backend setup. A presence check and core requirements fallback allowed context creation. Suggested consolidation: gate extension-backed Vulkan entry points on both capability and loaded function availability.

title: Align FidelityFX Vulkan effect contexts in scratch storage
body: FidelityFX EffectContext is alignas(32), but the backend lays it after uint32_t-aligned arrays and maps the raw address without realignment; context initialization read misaligned scratch and crashed on Dozen. I had to add absolute-address alignment and reserve up to alignof(EffectContext)-1 bytes in the scratch-size calculation. Suggested consolidation: make the scratch layout allocator encode each type's alignment and size.

title: Model FSR3 provider-owned shared temporal outputs
body: Fsr3Upscaler had to allocate Vulkan images and device memory for dilated depth, dilated motion vectors, and reconstructed previous nearest depth, then rotate four sets to match frames in flight, because the provider contract only exposes graph inputs and output. Suggested consolidation: add a declared provider shared-resource allocation/lifetime seam so backend-owned temporal outputs are described and synchronized through the facade.

title: Pass the Undertow root into VIXEN CMake regeneration
body: CMake regeneration failed with Text requires UNDERTOW_ROOT. Setting UNDERTOW_ROOT=/home/liory/projects/undertow before the same queued cmake --build build/wsl invocation allowed configure and build to complete. Suggested consolidation: resolve the Undertow root from the checkout or document and validate it in the canonical queued build entry point.

title: Expose direct GPU timestamps for provider execution spans
body: The existing VIXEN performance CSV emitted zero for every GPU timing column on the WSL Dozen driver, including whole-frame and fsr3_temporal_ms, so I added an opt-in Vulkan timestamp query pool around the FSR3 dispatch to measure its actual command span. Suggested consolidation: make the shared GPU query/readback telemetry return valid per-stage timings on supported Vulkan drivers, with a documented fallback when it cannot.

title: Account for WSL-invoked FidelityFX shader compiler CPU in queue watchdog
body: The queued WSL build command UNDERTOW_ROOT=/home/liory/projects/undertow bash /home/liory/.local/bin/with-test-lock.sh --agent fsr3 --resource build --label fsr3:runtime-profile-build2-undertow-root -- nice -n 10 cmake --build build/wsl --target VIXEN test_upscaler_selection VulkanResources test_vulkanresources_basic -j4 exited 75 after 231 seconds idle at FSR3 shader generation. CMake launches the SDK PE FidelityFX_SC.exe through WSL /init, so its Windows CPU work is invisible to Linux procfs and the queue idle watchdog killed the payload. The retry through the same queue with two jobs has progressed through shader generation. Suggested consolidation: make the canonical VIXEN WSL build route declare CPU use for this external compiler or avoid the cross-platform subprocess.
